question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,0]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)={y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-3y. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,2]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-0.2,\,1.2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**
${x}_{2}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-3y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{3}-{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-3y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2xy-4x \\ 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2xy-4x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(-2xy-4x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2y-4 & -2x \\ -2x & 6y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}-2y-4 & -2x \\ -2x & 6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-2xy-4x \\ 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}-2y-4 & -2x \\ -2x & 6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-2xy-4x \\ 3{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-3\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-0.2 \\ 1.2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-2(1.2)-4 & -2(-0.2) \\ -2(-0.2) & 6(1.2)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-2(-0.2)(1.2)-4(-0.2) \\ 3(1.2)^{2}-(-0.2)^{2}-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-0.2 \\ 1.2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-6.4 & 0.4 \\ 0.4 & 7.2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1.28 \\ 1.28\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-0.2 \\ 1.2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-6.4)\cdot 7.2-0.4\cdot 0.4}[\begin{aligned}7.2 & -0.4 \\ -0.4 & -6.4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1.28 \\ 1.28\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-0.2 \\ 1.2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{46.24}[\begin{aligned}8.704 \\ -8.704\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.012 \\ 1.012\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
